dimensions.assessment: The bill directs federal departments to develop a strategy and engage internationally, affecting federal agencies and nuclear sector entities in the United States and Europe.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Energy and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, shall develop a strategy

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes significant funding and strategic planning to alter energy security and nuclear cooperation dynamics across Europe and counter foreign influence.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029 to support critically needed engagement in Europe

dimensions.assessment: Appropriates $30 million per year for five fiscal years (2025 through 2029), totaling $150 million in authorized funding.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029

dimensions.assessment: Requires a comprehensive interagency strategy covering reactor types, fuel cycles, diplomatic engagements, and country-specific analyses.

dimensions.assessment: Mandates a one-time strategy report submission within 120 days alongside authorizations spanning a five-year period.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill authorizes $30,000,000 annually from fiscal years 2025 through 2029 for engagement and capacity building in Europe related to nuclear energy cooperation and countering Russian malign influence, and requires a detailed federal strategy within 120 days.

card.summary: H.R. 2913, the Ukraine Support Act, addresses the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine by authorizing various forms of economic, diplomatic, and military assistance for Ukraine and allied European nations, while establishing mandatory sanctions, export controls, and import restrictions against Russia and certain foreign actors if specific triggers related to Russian aggression are met.
